passage:
In the Pune hostel, Jeevan scrolled through photos: Farhan by a frozen lake, Farhan in a bright new flat, Farhan with a coffee and a snowy street. Every post had a caption like "Best decision ever."
That night Jeevan opened the same country's application page and paid the fee. It took two weeks of exam preparation and most of a month's pocket money.
When Jeevan's mother asked, "Why that country?" the answer came out thin: "Everyone is going." She waited. Jeevan could not name one reason that was Jeevan's own, not even the cold, which Jeevan hated.
Farhan messaged later: "Honestly, the photos are just the good hours." Jeevan stared at the message for a long while.

qa.q: Where does Jeevan live in the passage?
qa.a: Jeevan lives in a hostel in Pune.

qa.q: What was Jeevan feeling while scrolling through Farhan's photos?
qa.a: Jeevan was envious and afraid of being left behind, which drove the quick application.

qa.q: What could Jeevan do now to see whether the country really fits?
qa.a: Jeevan could write down personal reasons and ask people living there what daily life is like, then decide.

qa.q: How might Farhan's photos differ from Farhan's daily life?
qa.a: Farhan says the photos are just the good hours, so the life behind them includes plain and harder times as well.

grounding: The passage shows a person seeing classmates' photos from abroad and applying to the same country without asking whether it fits, so social comparison drives the choice.

passage:
'Why Australia, Nazia?' Shreya asked, looking at the offer letter on the table.
'Because Ayan's there, and Rukhsar, and half our batch. Did you see Ayan's beach photos?'
'I saw. But what do you want there?'
'A job. A life. Same as them.'
'You hate heat. Last month you told me you wanted a master's in urban design. Is that even there?'
'I'll figure it out when I land.'
Six months later, on a video call at 3 a.m. in Brisbane, Shreya watched her sister cry into a sleeve.
'Ayan's in Perth. Nobody I know is even in this city. The job is warehouse shifts, the course I wanted is in Europe, and I spent all my savings getting here.'
'Come home?'
'I don't know. I don't know anything.'

qa.q: Where is Ayan, according to Nazia on the call?
qa.a: Ayan is in Perth, while Nazia is in Brisbane.

qa.q: What was Nazia feeling on the 3 a.m. call?
qa.a: Nazia was lonely, lost and regretful, far from friends and stuck in work that didn't match what she wanted.

qa.q: What other approach could Nazia have used before accepting?
qa.a: Nazia could have listed what she wanted, like the urban design course and a cooler climate, and checked which country fit, instead of following friends' photos.

qa.q: How might Shreya feel watching her sister cry?
qa.a: Shreya is probably worried and sad, and maybe frustrated that her early questions weren't taken seriously.

grounding: It shows a young woman choosing a country because classmates moved there, not because it fits her, and paying for it later.

passage:
My name is Ramesh, and I applied to Canada for one reason: Jasleen's photos. She had moved to Toronto with three others from our college, and every week there was snow, a new apartment, a group dinner. I didn't ask myself if I liked cold, or big cities, or starting over in a field where my degree wasn't recognised. I copied their consultant, their course, even their intake month.
When I landed, the course had little to do with my field, and my friends were so busy with their own shifts that I saw Jasleen twice in four months. Photos don't show rent. They don't show someone crying in a laundry room either.
I'm still here, trying to fix it. But if my cousin asks me next year, I'll ask one question first: what do you want, not what do they have?

qa.q: How many times did Ramesh see Jasleen in four months?
What does Ramesh's line about the laundry room suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Ramesh has felt lonely and overwhelmed, hurt that the reality was so different from the photos.

qa.q: What would Ramesh have the cousin do differently?
qa.a: Start with what the cousin wants from life and work, and check whether a country fits that, instead of copying friends' choices.

qa.q: How might Jasleen see her photos now?
qa.a: Jasleen may not have realised how her posts influenced Ramesh, and might feel a pang knowing the photos hid the hard parts.

grounding: It shows someone applying to the same country as classmates because of their photos, letting comparison drive the choice, and struggling after arriving.
